context: Wilde to Frank Harris, [? circa 3 March 1898], Hotel de Nice, Paris. Ten months out of prison, asking for £5. Headed with his exile name, and closing on the dinner Harris had invited him to while he was still in Reading Gaol.
quote:
From Sebastian Melmoth

Hotel de Nice, Rue des Beaux-Arts, Paris

My dear Frank, You have been so good and generous to me that I hate to have to ask you to be generous again — But I am entirely without money — and if you could let me have £5 you would be doing me a great kindness — I have had no money from my trustees for six months — and am trying to get back my little £3 a week, thro’ Robbie Ross, always a good friend to me — but there are delays, and in the meanwhile I drift in ridiculous impecuniosity — without a sou. So, if you can, do something.

I long to see you here — and to have the dinner you asked me to at _Reading_ —

Ever yours Oscar Wilde
original_provenance: Read at HRC 2676, images 82-83 - one bifolium: image 82 shows sides 4 (left) and 1 (right), image 83 the inner opening, sides 2 and 3. Signed 'Oscar Wilde' in full. Heading: 'From Sebastian Melmoth', his exile name, written above the address and ruled off with a long stroke. The volume drops it entirely and heads the letter 'Hotel de Nice'. It is the only letter in this folder where he uses the name. Emphasis: '_Reading_' on the last side, followed by one of his long dashes; confirmed by Lovelle 2026-08-10. Nothing else on the four sides is underlined. The mark is where the irony sits - the dinner Harris asked him to at Reading was asked while he was in Reading Gaol. The volume sets it in italic and keeps it, which is right. 1173). This one rises left to right and sweeps, and is a genuine underline all the same. So stroke shape does not settle it; length against the word does, plus the ink and the weight. Other hands: '£8.8.0' in pencil at the head, a circled 'E' in the top corner, and '(Harris)' in pencil after 'My dear Frank' - a later identification, not Wilde's. Punctuation: his dashes restored; 'thro'' is his contraction, expanded to 'through' in the volume.
